metaDescription: Male infertility evaluation, semen analysis review, varicocele assessment, hormone testing, treatment options, and follow-up care with Dr. Vikram.

hero.title: Male infertility
hero.summary: Understand semen analysis, low sperm count, varicocele, hormones, obstruction, sexual health, treatment options, and next steps.

body: Male infertility means difficulty contributing to pregnancy. It may be linked to sperm count, sperm movement, sperm shape, hormones, varicocele, infection, obstruction, ejaculation problems, or sexual function.
Many men feel stressed or embarrassed. A private and structured evaluation can reduce confusion and show the right next step.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Many men have no clear symptoms except difficulty conceiving. Some may have testicular pain, swelling, small testes, low sexual desire, erection concerns, ejaculation problems, or a known varicocele.
An abnormal semen analysis is often the first clue.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if pregnancy has not happened after regular trying, semen analysis is abnormal, varicocele is present, or there is testicular pain or swelling.
You should also consult if there is erectile dysfunction, ejaculation difficulty, low desire, past testicular surgery, infection, or injury.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Tests may include semen analysis, repeat semen analysis, hormone tests, scrotal ultrasound, infection tests, genetic tests in selected cases, and physical examination.
The aim is to identify treatable causes and plan realistic fertility options.

experience.title: Treatment options for male infertility
body: Treatment depends on semen results, hormones, examination, varicocele status, sexual function, and partner factors.
Options may include lifestyle changes, medicines, hormone correction, infection treatment, varicocele surgery, sperm retrieval, or assisted reproduction coordination.

careGuide.title: Before, during, and after fertility care
careGuide.intro: Male infertility care works best when reports, history, and goals are reviewed together.

tabs.label: Before Treatment
items: Note how long you have been trying
Bring hormone reports or ultrasound if available
Write down questions with your partner if possible

tabs.label: After Treatment
items: Discuss next options if results do not improve

careGuide.note: Your plan will depend on test results, examination, partner factors, and fertility goals.

items.question: Is male infertility common?
items.answer: Yes. Male factors contribute to many fertility challenges.

items.question: Is one semen analysis enough?
items.answer: Not always. Semen results can vary. A repeat test may be advised.

items.question: Can varicocele affect fertility?
items.answer: Varicocele can affect sperm quality in some men. Treatment depends on reports, examination, and goals.

items.question: Can lifestyle changes help?
items.answer: Smoking, alcohol, heat exposure, weight, sleep, and some medicines can affect fertility.

items.question: Is consultation private?
items.answer: Yes. Fertility and sexual health concerns are handled confidentially and respectfully.
